title: Policy merge ordering bug causes tenant tier demotion during capacity rebalances
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity rebalance event in Dedicated and Private clusters, a nondeterministic ordering bug in the policy-merge code caused tenant-specific fallback entries to be merged ahead of higher-priority tier pins. The effect: requests were routed to lower-cost/low-tier model replicas (tier demotion) or to a regional fallback, producing increased latency and degraded model outputs for several customers.

Observed impact: 3 enterprise tenants reported a sudden drop in latency SLA compliance and a spike in error rates when autoscaler triggered rebalance. Some requests were served by quantized variants incompatible with tenant AV requirements, causing degraded output quality and customer escalations.

Scope: Affects hosted routing controller (policy merge path) and Dedicated/Private routing agents during rebalance/scale-down windows. Not a model runtime bug; routing decision layer only.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate capacity rebalance: initiate autoscaler scale-down on a Dedicated pool with mixed tier assignments
Deploy a conflicting tenant override and a global fallback with overlapping regions
Replay production traffic pattern with KV-cache cold start and concurrent policy-refresh events
Observe routing decisions in router logs: verify fallback entry ordering and resulting target tier/model selection
root_cause: The policy-merge implementation used a hash-map iteration order that is nondeterministic across runs. During a rebalance, concurrent policy-refresh and tenant-override writes caused a race where fallback entries were inserted before tenant tier pins. The merge algorithm did not enforce explicit priority keys during reduce, allowing lower-priority entries to win when maps were merged in different iteration orders.
mitigation: Applied emergency routing override: set 'prefer_tenant_pin' flag at control plane (hotfix) to force tenant pins to take precedence. Scoped override rolled out to affected regions within 12 minutes. Also opened a temporary admission-rule to reject policy updates that change fallback priorities during rebalance windows.
fix_plan: 1) Replace map-based merge with deterministic ordered-merge that sorts by explicit priority and timestamp. 2) Add unit tests and property tests to assert commutativity and idempotence of merges. 3) Add e2e scenario in integration harness to simulate concurrent policy updates under rebalance. 4) Backport fix to runtime-1.20 and runtime-1.22 branches and ship hotfix. 5) Rollforward with canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback hooks.
deployment_note: Canary on Dedicated US-west clusters only for initial verification. Watch metrics: misroute_rate, sloa_violations, routing_latency_ms, and model_compatibility_error. Expected safe window: 2 hours per canary stage. Coordinate with SRE for autoscaler freeze during rollout of the control-plane change.
qa_checks: Integration test: reproducible deterministic merge order across 1000 random seeds
E2E: run rebalance scenario with production trace and assert no tenant demotions
Regression: ensure KV cache reuse and batching unaffected (compare token latency baseline)
Canary metrics: misroute_rate < 0.01% and sloa_violations not increasing
